raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year the way I always do — one crop at a time, starting with what's already in the ground.

---

**The wheat first.** I planted it back in mid-October like always. Five mu isn't much, but it's enough to worry about. I used the same variety the seed shop sells everyone around here — I forget the number, something like Jimai 22 or whatever they had, my neighbor's son picks it up for me when he goes. About 15 kg seed per mu, cost me around 35 yuan per mu. I don't save seed anymore, hasn't been worth it for years.

Before planting I spread compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind, about 40 kg per mu as base. That's my habit. The extension station man came around a few years back and said we were over-applying, but when I tried cutting back one year the wheat looked yellow and I got scared, so I went back to my old amount. My husband works in town most of the year so I don't have anyone to argue with about it.

For topdressing at jointing (around early March), I put down urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. If the wheat looks strong I do less, if it looks weak I do more. This year it came through winter okay so I'll stick with my usual.

Irrigation — I'll do winter water in late November (already did it actually), then green-up water in March, jointing water, and grain-filling water. Four times. The well is ours jointly with two other households and the electricity bill has gone up, so I watch the weather. If it rains good in spring I'll skip one. Each irrigation costs me maybe 40 yuan per mu with the electricity.

Herbicide I spray once in spring against the grassy weeds. Cheap stuff, maybe 20 yuan per mu. No insecticide unless aphids show up bad at heading — then I'll spray once.

I expect about 430 kg/mu. That's what I usually get. Last year was 450, the year before was 400 because of the late frost. 430 is a fair guess.

---

**Then the maize.** Right after wheat harvest in early June — and I mean RIGHT after, because the next day someone comes with the machine to seed maize directly into the stubble. No tillage, it's been this way for years in our village. Every hour matters, the maize needs heat units.

Hybrid seed, I'll use Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop recommends this year — about 50 yuan per mu, you have to buy new every year for hybrids. I know some farmers tried that Denghai variety, neighbor said it did well, I might try one mu of it if the shop has it, but I'm not changing everything.

Fertilizer — I put about 25 kg of compound with the seeder as starter, then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage, maybe 15 kg per mu. That's roughly 13-14 kg N per mu total, I think? The extension people said to split it more but it's hard when I'm alone in the field, one topdress is enough work for me.

Maize I irrigate less. Usually once at tasseling if July is dry. Summer rain is usually enough. Some years I don't irrigate at all.

Herbicide right after seeding is important for maize, otherwise the weeds take over. I spray that for sure. Pests — the corn borer can be bad, I'll spray once if I see them.

Expect about 480 kg/mu. Maize here does better than wheat most years.

---

**The big picture.** My son sends money sometimes, my husband's factory wages cover household expenses, so the farm income isn't our only lifeline — but it's still real money, and the 5 mu feeds us grain too. I keep some wheat and maize for the family and sell the rest. Total input costs this year I figure around 3,000 yuan for the whole 5 mu across both crops. I could spend more and maybe get more yield, but I've done this 30 years and I know what works on my land.

My biggest worry is labor. I'm 57 and bending over in the field isn't what it was. If hired labor gets more expensive for harvest I'll feel it. But the combine comes through the village for both wheat and maize so that's manageable.
